name: Marquis de Morès
role: Founder of Medora; president of the N. P. Refrigerator Car Co.
bio: The Cow Boy described the Marquis de Morès as a young Frenchman, son-in-law of the New York banker von Hoffman, who had bought large stretches of grazing land on the Little Missouri. In early 1884 he traveled to Washington about a freight and mail route to Deadwood, and that April he rode to Deadwood with Joe Pennell, making the return ride in twenty-six hours, and agreed to put on a stage line from Medora to Deadwood. He signed company notices as president, and in October 1884 ordered 200 cords of stone for a new refrigerator and received an order for 500 cattle from a Chicago firm. Alfalfa seed arrived for experiments in his garden in June 1884, and in 1885 believed he had found kaolin clay near Medora. In March 1885 the paper announced the birth of his son, and in September 1885 he stood trial at Bismarck over the killing of Luffsey, with defense witnesses testifying that Luffsey and O'Donald had threatened to shoot him on sight. In January 1886 he returned from France, and in October 1886 the paper credited him and Theodore Roosevelt, as Dakota members of the Montana Stockgrowers' Association executive committee, with quick action against a cattle disease.
